name: NVIDIA Corp
day_summary: NVDA rallied +1.72% to $198.32 on quarter-end risk-on — but the exit executed at the open as mandated, and the $200 re-entry gate held as resistance. SPX closed ~7,525, clearing the regime gate for the first time since the May 14 ATH, but NVDA still sits $1.68 below the threshold that would trigger a re-entry signal.
long_pnl: Longs who held through the stop-day exit missed a +1.72% day — exit was mandatory after Stop Day 2 triggered at yesterday's $194.97 close ($0.03 below the $195 stop line).
short_pnl: Shorts gave back ground on the quarter-end rally; puts expired worthless on a tape that gapped higher into the close of Q2.

decision.horizon: FLAT/CASH — Exit protocol fully executed at the June 30 open (Stop Day 2 triggered). SPX cleared the 7,460 regime gate (~7,525 close), but NVDA at $198.32 is $1.68 below the $200 volume-confirmed re-entry threshold. All three gates must clear simultaneously: (1) SPX > 7,460 on closing basis ✓, (2) VIX < 17 on closing basis ✓ (est. ~16), (3) NVDA > $200 on above-average volume (>200M shares) ✗. NFP on July 2 into a 3-day holiday gap (July 4–6) keeps macro risk elevated. Earliest viable full re-entry: July 7–8 post-NFP resolution.

Options flow is split: aggressive writers sold puts at $195 (expecting the floor holds) while cautious longs bought $195/$190 put spreads for NFP protection. The exit overhang is cleared; the market is now watching for a catalyst (earnings estimate revisions, Blackwell demand update, or post-NFP macro lift) to push NVDA through $200 on conviction volume.

analysis:
## Technical analysis

**Trend:** NVDA remains in a recovery channel from the $142.03 52-week low, but the rally has stalled in a $188–$200 consolidation range for the past two weeks. The May 14 ATH at $236.54 is $38.22 away — meaningful overhead supply exists at every $10 increment ($200, $210, $220). Today's close of $198.32 keeps NVDA inside this consolidation box.

**Momentum:** RSI estimated ~52 (neutral; not overbought). The quarter-end +1.72% day is welcome but did not produce a momentum breakout — volume at ~185M shares is below the >200M threshold required for a re-entry signal. MACD is flat-positive, suggesting consolidation rather than trending impulse.

**Volume:** ~185M shares traded — below average. This is critical: the re-entry gate explicitly requires above-average volume (>200M) on a $200+ close. Today's volume confirms the market is not yet prepared to make a sustained commitment above $200. Quarter-end rebalancing flows inflate the volume denominator for recent sessions.

**Key levels with evidence:**
- **★ Strongest resistance: $200.** Acted as the precise intraday high lid ($200.01) on the best quarter-end tape in six years. Has rejected NVDA three times in the past two weeks. The re-entry protocol designates $200 as the gate — the market is treating it as a meaningful level.
- **★ Strongest support: $192.53** (June 26 correction low). Held on the highest-volume day of the past month (Russell reconstitution). Has not been retested since; represents the floor of the current consolidation base.

**Protocol status:** Stop Day 2 triggered on June 29 ($194.97, $0.03 below $195 stop line). Exit executed at the June 30 open per mandatory protocol. Three re-entry gates: (1) SPX > 7,460 ✓ cleared today; (2) VIX < 17 ✓ cleared today (~16 est.); (3) NVDA > $200 on >200M shares ✗ not yet cleared. Gates (1) and (2) are open for the first time since the May 14 ATH; gate (3) is the only remaining barrier.

**Risk:** NFP July 2 into a 3-day US holiday gap (July 4–6) means the re-entry gate cannot be tested again until July 7 at the earliest. A hot NFP print could reprice rates and re-open the VIX/SPX gates; a cold print could accelerate the $200 break. Position: cash.
